physics_goals.quote: Gluonic excitations, the physics of strange and charm quarks and nucleon structure studies will be performed with unprecedented accuracy
physics_goals.value: Study the strong interaction with antiprotons: gluonic excitations, strange and charm quark physics and nucleon structure

summary.plain: PANDA is a planned detector at the future FAIR facility that will collide antiprotons with a hydrogen target to study how quarks and gluons form hadrons. It will search for exotic particles such as glueballs and hybrids, charm spectroscopy, hypernuclei and nucleon structure.
summary.technical: Antiproton ANnihilations at DArmstadt: internal-target detector at the High Energy Storage Ring (HESR) with a target spectrometer (solenoid) and a forward spectrometer (dipole) for precision charmonium and open-charm spectroscopy, glueball and hybrid searches, hadrons in matter, hypernuclei and nucleon structure; the PANDA collaboration has more than 420 scientists from 18 countries.
